NOTICE AND AGENDA

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  John P. Ramirez, AICP, Director of Community Development

SUBJECT: NORWALK TRANSIT VILLAGE PROJECT UPDATE – CITY PROJECT
  NO. 7859

Background:

The former California Youth Authority project site (13200 Bloomfield Avenue) is
approximately 32 acres and is surrounded by residential development to the north, west,
and south, and Zimmerman Park and the Metrolink rail line to the east. Given the
surrounding uses and the close proximity to transit, there is a great opportunity to develop
a transit-oriented eco community by redeveloping this site with diverse housing choices
while providing significant neighborhood amenities, including a direct connection to the
transit line. In order to create a project that is inclusive and reflects the Norwalk
community, the project team has kicked off public outreach efforts and incorporated the
feedback received into a developing vision and conceptual site plan for the Norwalk
Transit Village. This item is an update and status report of that vision and concept plan.

Discussion

With COVID-19 and the emergence of the Omicron variant, to date the majority of the
public outreach that has been conducted was virtual. However, there were two in-person
outreach events, which drew significant interest from the community. An interactive
Farmer’s Market booth and an informal series of presentations to members of the City’s
various commissions took place in January 2022 and February 2022. In addition, a
steering committee made up of community residents and other stakeholders was formed
to help provide additional insight into the future development of the site.

A summary of the community engagement efforts to date are summarized below:
  • Project website launched: www.NorwalkTransitVillage.com
  • Nine social media posts across three platforms with over 200 engagements
  • Three email blasts to over 1,100 residents surrounding the site
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Norwalk Transit Village Project Update  Page No. 2

  •  Three text message blasts to over 1,900 residents surrounding the site
  •  Over 10 stakeholder meetings that engaged about 50 people
  •  Over 500 mailers and surveys sent to neighboring stakeholders
  •  Connected with over 200 residents at the Farmer’s Market

Community Feedback

Generally, the community had a positive reaction to the project and has voiced support
for building more affordable housing in Norwalk and improving connectivity between the
project site to Zimmerman Park and the Metrolink Station. Suggestions regarding the
commercial portion of the project included grocery options as well as food and beverage
options that keep people in the community instead of traveling to neighboring cities.

The following key elements and themes have been identified for project consideration by
the community:
  • Preservation and enhancement of Zimmerman Park
  • Improved connectivity to Zimmerman Park and Metrolink Station
  • New community park
  • Community-oriented commercial uses
  • Adequate buffers from surrounding properties
  • Palette of housing types and affordable housing
  • Multimodal streets and varying street types

Next Steps

The project team will continue to incorporate the public feedback received, the goals of a
transit-oriented eco village, and State requirements from both the California Department
of Housing and Community Development and Surplus Land Act into a vision and draft
plans for the Norwalk Transit Village. Once a land plan is established, the project team
will kick off the specific plan and environmental analysis of the project. The entitlements
are expected to be approved in early Spring 2023.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s Strategic Plan Goal 3: Partner with our
stakeholders to create and sustain a resilient and economically prosperous city with
opportunity for everyone as it would build a great public destination.
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Norwalk Transit Village Project Update  Page No. 3

Recommended Action:

Staff is seeking feedback on the draft vision of the project.

Attachments: N/A

SUBJECT: PARK PROJECTS UPDATE

Background:

The City operates and maintains 12 parks citywide. Currently, there are park projects at
several parks in various stages of work, from requested funding/waiting for notification, to
design, to construction. Each park provides opportunities and challenges, with staff
always looking for new funding sources for additional projects and upgrades. Each park
is listed below with funded and proposed projects, as well as requested funding sources,
and future projects which require funding.

Bob White Park

Bob White Park includes the Shoshonean Campsite, a basketball court, a playground,
horseshoe pits, and a picnic area. The campsite is rented four to six times per year from
various groups, and portable restrooms are provided as part of the rental fee.
In November 2021, City Council approved moving forward with the installation of a
restroom building and dog park through Proposition (Prop) 68 per capita funds. The funds
are administered by the State in the form of a grant and an application was submitted for
$243,000, and it is anticipated that the funding approval will be received in the coming
weeks.

Additionally, a funding request of $450,000 was submitted in May 2021 to Senator
Archuleta’s office to construct a playground, provide Americans with Disabilities (ADA)
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Park Projects Update  Page No. 2

upgrades, picnic areas, benches, trash cans, and installation of lighting for the basketball
court.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Installation of parking lot lighting  $100,000
  •  LED lighting for campsite and dog park  $ 60,000
  •  Installation of block wall along the railroad for campsite and park  $ 94,000

Approved budget funding:  $0
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $693,000
Future projects funding requests:  $254,000

Gerdes Park

Gerdes Park provides ballfields, handball and basketball courts, playground, spray pool,
and MPR building. Ballfield lighting will be added to the main ballfield at the park. Design
work is being completed and the project is due to be bid in late spring. Capital
Improvement Project (CIP) No. 7365 has $300,000 budgeted for this project. This project
will increase play time capacity of three to four hours per day, five to six days per week
for the leagues.

Funding of $7,000 is included in the Fiscal Year (FY) 2021/22 budget for laser leveling of
the ballfield, which is a maintenance item and will be completed in the coming months.

A new playground was installed in 2014. Additional rehabilitation work in recent years
includes remodeling of restrooms, painting of the handball courts, a sports-themed mural
added to the back side of the courts, painting of the basketball court surface, and addition
of picnic areas.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Convert spray pool to splash pad to allow for use  $ 25,000
  •  Replacement of scoreboard  $ 12,000
  •  Remodel snack bar and add grease interceptor  $ 65,000
  •  Pour N Play surface for playground  $ 75,000
  •  Install block wall at parking lot/apartments, update landscaping  $ 31,000

Approved budget funding:  $307,000
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $0
Future projects funding requests:  $208,000
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Park Projects Update  Page No. 3

Glazier Park

Glazier Park amenities include a basketball court, playground, and shaded picnic area.
Improvements in recent years include the addition of an art piece in 2014, a new
playground in 2017, a park monument sign, remodeling of restrooms, and rehabilitation
of the covered picnic area on the north side of the park.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Installation of pergola for BBQ area adjacent to building  $ 20,000
  •  Pour N Play surface for playground  $ 75,000
  •  Add block wall to Excelsior Greenbelt residential area  $ 60,000

Approved budget funding:  $0
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $0
Future projects funding requests:  $155,000

Holifield Park

Holifield Park provides three baseball fields, two playgrounds, basketball court, two snack
bars, and restroom/maintenance facilities. One of the playgrounds was recently replaced,
funded through the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors at the request of Supervisor
Janice Hahn. Due to the placement of the playground, a large open area was created
which has been evaluated for installation of a skate park similar in size to the existing
location at Norwalk Park that is being removed. The area would be highly visible from
Excelsior Drive and would be near the Recreation building, providing staff the ability to
monitor the skate park when the park is staffed.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Installation of concrete skate park  $700,000
  •  Replace roof for main snack bar  $100,000
  •  Replace second playground near ballfields  $400,000
  •  Upgrade walkway lights to LED  $ 40,000
  •  Convert ballfield lighting to LED  $450,000
  •  Parking lot slurry seal (dependent on Tank Farm development)  $ 75,000

Approved budget funding:  $0
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $0
Future projects funding requests:  $1,765,000
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Park Projects Update  Page No. 4

Lakeside Park

Lakeside Park has two ballfields, a snack bar, and a playground. Restrooms were
remodeled several years ago and landscaped planters were added to the park.

Funding of $14,000 is approved in the FY 2021/22 budget for laser leveling of ballfields
at the park, which will be completed in the coming months.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Installation of ballfield lighting – 2 fields  $750,000
  •  Pour N Play surface for playground  $ 75,000

Approved budget funding:  $14,000
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $0
Future projects funding requests:  $825,000

New River Park

New River Park provides a small restroom/activity building, a walking path, and a
playground. In 2020, a monument sign was added to the southwest corner of the park.
Other recent improvements include remodeling of restrooms and landscape upgrades.
Work is also ongoing to replace walkway areas that have damaged concrete.

A funding request for $300,000 was submitted in May 2021 to Senator Archuleta’s office
to construct a new playground.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Installation of Pergola picnic area  $ 40,000

Approved budget funding:  $0
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $300,000
Future projects funding requests:  $40,000

Ramona Park

Ramona Park has a playground, large covered picnic area, basketball court, activity room,
handball court area, and a ballfield.

Funding of $7,000 is approved in the FY 2021/22 budget for laser leveling of the ballfield
at the park, which will be completed in the coming months.
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Park Projects Update  Page No. 5

In addition to remodeling of restrooms and painting of the handball courts, the playground
was replaced in 2016, and in 2020, a monument sign was added to the east entrance of
the park.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Installation of ballfield lights  $350,000
  •  Pour N Play surface for playground  $ 75,000
  •  Installation of shade pergola adjacent to building  $ 30,000

Approved budget funding:  $7,000
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $0
Future projects funding requests:  $455,000

Sara Mendez Park

Sara Mendez Park provides an activity room, two restroom facilities, a walking path with
picnic and exercise station areas, and a splash pad. Due to construction of the I-5
freeway, the City received funds from Caltrans to offset the area that was utilized for
construction. Several improvements were completed at the park, including installation of
fitness equipment and picnic table areas around the walking track, concrete work, and
landscaping improvements. A balance of $100,000 remains and staff are evaluating the
expansion of the patio area to accommodate larger groups for rentals. The work will
include a pergola area, additional picnic tables, and a built in patio BBQ/serving station.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Replace damaged splash pad controller  $ 5,000

Approved budget funding:  $100,000
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $0
Future projects funding requests:  $5,000

Vista Verde Park

Vista Verde Park provides an activity building, playground, splash pad, handball courts,
and a basketball court. Recent improvements to the park include additional picnic areas,
refurbishment of the artwork near the splash pad, painting of the handball courts, and
installation of a park monument sign in 2016.

A funding request for $350,000 was submitted in May 2021 to Senator Archuleta’s office
to construct a new playground.
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Park Projects Update  Page No. 6

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  LED lighting upgrades for basketball court and playground  $ 25,000
  •  Addition of a shaded pergola to the building  $ 12,000
  •  Installation of a block wall along the north end of the park  $138,000
  along the railroad

Approved budget funding:  $0
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $350,000
Future projects funding requests:  $175,000

Zimmerman Park

Zimmerman Park is utilized as a sports park. It has three ballfields, a snack bar, a
playground, and a small basketball court. The snack bar and restrooms were remodeled,
along with the addition of a walking path at the park, and installation of fitness equipment.

Funding of $21,000 is included in the FY 2021/22 budget for laser leveling of the ballfield
at the park, which will be completed in the coming months.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  LED lighting upgrades for basketball court and playground  $ 25,000
  •  Convert ballfield lighting to LED  $360,000
  •  Installation of a block wall along the north end of the park  $ 85,000
  along the railroad
  •  Snack Bar remodel  $ 30,000

Approved budget funding:  $21,000
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $0
Future projects funding requests:  $500,000

Norwalk Park

Norwalk Park incorporates a variety of facilities, including the Norwalk Arts and Sports
Complex, Cultural Arts Center, Aquatics Center, Teen Center, Sproul Reception Center,
and the Sproul Museum. The park has a large picnic area, restroom, and storage facility,
playground, basketball courts, and walking paths. A Master Plan is in the process of
being developed for Norwalk Park, which includes new sports fields, playgrounds, an
additional restroom facility, and a variety of park amenities. CIP No. 7363 is currently
funded with $300,000 for replacement of the existing playground.
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Park Projects Update  Page No. 7

A funding request for $1.3 million was submitted in May 2021 to Senator Archuleta’s office
to construct a playground, restroom facilities, and various amenities at the southwest
corner of the park. Caltrans will be deeding two vacant parcels at this location to the City
to be used to expand Norwalk Park. If approved, the project would be incorporated with
the approved $300,000 CIP for a total of $1.6 million.

Removal of the skate park was approved in November 2021, and is in process. The area
will create an opportunity to expand the Sproul Reception Center to create a larger venue
for weddings and events if approved. The area is adjacent to the Sproul Museum, which
requires extensive work if it is to remain open to the public, or incorporate the space and
utilize it as a “Bride Room” or staging area for events.

If approved by City Council, it is staff’s recommendation to apply for a Proposition (Prop)
68 grant to redesign and rehabilitate Norwalk Park. The maximum grant award would be
$8.5 million and the City would be responsible for the remaining $3.5 million balance
estimate.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Rehabilitate Norwalk Park – Develop Master Design  $12,000,000
  •  Expand Sproul Reception Center  $2,000,000
  (Estimate may fluctuate based on expansion options)
  •  Remodel park restrooms near Teen Center  $ 200,000
  (Option if not moving forward with Park Master Design Plan/Grant)
  •  Installation of remaining LED walkway lights in the park  $ 15,000
  (Lights along Sproul Street upgraded in 2019/20)
  •  Rehabilitate Sproul Museum (if it remains public museum)  $ 300,000

Approved budget funding:  $300,000
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $1,300,000
Future projects funding requests:  $2,000,000 - $14,000,000
  (Depending on City Council direction)

Hermosillo Park

Hermosillo Park Master Plan was approved by City Council in 2019. The City has been
awarded an $8.5 million grant through Prop 68 to rehabilitate the park. Funding includes
the construction of a new community building, restrooms, parking lot, and various
amenities throughout the park. The playground was replaced in 2018 and will remain in
place, but a Pour N Play surface will be installed as part of the overall project. Measure
A funding in the amount of $2.2 million is available to include in the project, as the initial
engineer’s estimate is approximately $10.6 million. An additional $75,000 is budgeted for
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Park Projects Update  Page No. 8

CIP No. 7359, restroom remodel, which was put on hold pending notification of the Prop
68 grant notification.

An underground storm water infiltration project has been approved and will soon begin
the design phase. Measure W funding in the amount of $23 million was awarded for the
project, which is expected to take three to four years for completion. $2.4 million of the
funds were recently received for the project.

Funding is included in the FY 2021/22 budget for laser leveling of ballfields at the park,
but with notification of the Prop 68 grant, this work will not go forward.

Future projects and estimated costs to be considered are:

  •  Install Pour N Play playground surface (Measure A funds)  $ 75,000
  •  Installation of Water Well #9 (southeast corner of park)  $3,100,000
  Includes telemetry system, backup generator, etc.
  Potential funding thru U.S. Army Corp of Engineers grant

Approved grant funding:  $33,775,000
Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $0
Future projects funding requests:  $3,175,000

Overall Funding for Parks:

  Approved budget and/or funding:  $34,587,000
  Requested funding through grants, etc.:  $ 2,643,000
  Future projects funding requests:  $21,557,000

Conclusion

The City has many options for projects at parks. Norwalk Park provides a unique
opportunity to expand services and create a larger rental venue. Hermosillo Park project
designs will be underway soon and construction should be able to begin by the end of the
year for the Prop 68 park rehabilitation project. The addition of ballfield lighting at parks
increases play time for leagues and upgrading existing ballfield lights to LED’s greatly
reduces maintenance and energy costs. Adding block walls in parks will provide better
security and decrease continued maintenance costs for repairs due to cut fences and
vandalism. The addition of Pour-N-Play surfaces for playgrounds creates a safer
environment for children and decreases staff time and maintenance. A Citywide Park
Master Design Plan would be an option to identify resident input, prioritize projects and,
set a timeline/path to upgrading parks. The estimated cost would be $250,000 -
$300,000.
 City Council  February 22, 2022
Park Projects Update  Page No. 9

Fiscal Impact:

Several projects are included in the current FY 2021/22 Adopted Budget. Prop 68 and
Measure A funds for Hermosillo Park will be brought before City Council for approval
soon. The Fund 743 – Park Renovation Fund balance is $795,000. Additional funding
would be required for projects if approved.

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s Strategic Plan Goal 2: Enhance
maintenance and beautification practices.

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends City Council:

  a. approve moving forward with budget-approved projects where applicable;
  b. prioritize future projects; and
  c. provide staff direction for Citywide Master Park Design Plan.
